criteria.description: Uses the prospective-hindsight framing ('it's the future, the launch failed — why?') to surface risks, not a generic 'what are the risks' list.
Classifies risks (Tigers / Paper Tigers / Elephants, or an equivalent that separates real threats, false alarms, and unspoken risks).
Rates risks by likelihood and impact (or similar) and focuses on the vital few rather than treating all equally.
Assigns a concrete mitigation and an owner to each risk that matters (not just a list of worries).
Covers non-technical failure modes too — e.g. adoption/value, GTM, support load, sales/pricing cannibalization, team/capacity, dependencies — not only engineering risk.
Explicitly surfaces at least one 'elephant' — a risk teams often privately know but don't say (e.g. free tier cannibalizing paid, no monetization path, support can't handle volume).
